summary: hotels search no longer requires its own independent manual login separate from `auth login --chrome`. Two fixes were tried live and disproven before landing on the one that works: (1) pointing agent-browser at the real Default Chrome profile via --profile silently falls back to an isolated temp profile when the user's real Chrome already holds that profile's lock; (2) seeding agent-browser's session with the JWT/_csrf cookies auth.go already extracts gets the cookies set successfully but Concur's server clears them on the next navigation -- confirmed even when every cookie including the Akamai bot-sensor ones (_abck, ak_bmsc, bm_sv, bm_sz) is copied, pointing to a device/TLS-fingerprint-level binding that cookie values cannot cross. The working fix (detectDedicatedConcurBrowser + activeCDPPort in hotels_search.go) CDP-*attaches* to an already-running, already-authenticated Chrome instance instead of copying anything -- confirmed live end-to-end: a Chrome instance launched with --remote-debugging-port, logged into Concur once, stayed authenticated when agent-browser attached via `--cdp <port>`, and a full hotels search ran to completion with zero manual login and real live results (Buffalo hotels, 2026-10-18 to 2026-10-25, identical results to a manually-logged-in run moments earlier). Opt-in and backward compatible: when no dedicated debug-enabled Chrome is detected on the probed ports (or CONCUR_CDP_PORT), the command falls back unchanged to its original isolated-profile-launch behavior and its own separate login.
reason: User asked to refine the CLI to not use two separate browser sessions, after hitting the friction firsthand: auth login --chrome (pycookiecheat, reads the user's regular Chrome cookie DB directly) and hotels search (agent-browser, drives its own bundled 'Chrome for Testing' binary in an isolated user-data-dir -- confirmed via ps aux to be a genuinely different executable from /Applications/Google Chrome.app, not just a different profile of the same browser) required two independent logins with no shared session. True unification via credential copying is blocked by what is almost certainly Akamai bot-mitigation device/fingerprint binding (this tenant has ak_bmsc/_abck per the Aug 12 discovery report, and the existing flights-hotels-search.json patch already documented Akamai gating the hotel shopping-session mutation more strictly than reads) -- attaching to a live session, rather than replaying its credentials elsewhere, is the only mechanism confirmed to survive that binding.

changes.description: Added concurCDPPortCandidates, activeCDPPort, and detectDedicatedConcurBrowser: probes agent-browser --cdp <port> get url against 9222/9333/9229 (or CONCUR_CDP_PORT) for an already-authenticated concursolutions.com session before the existing isolated-launch flow runs. runAgentBrowser now prefixes every call with --cdp <port> when a dedicated browser was detected. The RunE flow's Step 1 sign-in check and its error message are updated to distinguish 'the dedicated browser's session expired, log in there again' from the original 'no dedicated browser found, use the isolated one's login' path, so the error message a user sees is always actionable for whichever transport is actually active. Long help text documents the one-time setup: create a real named Chrome profile (Chrome's own 'Add Person' UI, not a throwaway --user-data-dir) so 'auth login --chrome --profile "<name>"' can read its cookies too, then launch that profile with --remote-debugging-port and --profile-directory and log in once. No changes were needed in auth.go or cookiejar.go -- the existing --profile flag on `auth login --chrome` already supports reading from any standard-location named Chrome profile, which is why the setup recommendation steers toward a real profile instead of a custom directory.

validated_outcome: go build, go vet ./..., and go test ./... (all packages) all clean. Live end-to-end: with all agent-browser sessions closed and a separate Chrome instance running on --remote-debugging-port=9333 (logged into Concur once, manually, as the one-time setup step), `hotels search --to Buffalo --check-in 2026-10-18 --check-out 2026-10-25 --yes` printed 'Using dedicated Concur browser on CDP port 9333 (no separate login needed)' and returned real live results (Residence Inn By Marriott Buffalo Downtown $1708.05, Courtyard By Marriott $2693.83, etc.) with zero manual browser interaction -- matching a prior manually-logged-in run's results. Fallback path (no dedicated browser running) re-verified unchanged: reverted to the original file first, confirmed it still builds/vets/tests clean, before layering the fix back in.
